title: KV index reordering during regional weight merge — incident retrospective
summary: During a regional, staggered weight merge of a new model variant we observed a small but high-severity class of decoding failures in production. A subset of requests returned garbled tokens (invalid subtoken sequences) resulting in user-facing output corruption and elevated 5xx/error signals for the /v1/generate route on two regions. Root cause was a race between asynchronous KV-prefetch index updates and in-flight microbatch ordering which allowed an outdated KV index to be used with newly merged weight shards, producing token-id mismatches.
timeline: 2024-11-07 10:12 UTC — Canary regional rollout started (eu-west-1) with staggered weight-merge plan
2024-11-07 10:26 UTC — First anomalous decode errors detected by alerting (tokenization-mismatch-alert) on eu-west-1; error rate 0.3%
2024-11-07 10:31 UTC — Ops triage: increased p95 latency and decoding errors observed on same route; initial suspicion: weight shard mapping mismatch
2024-11-07 10:35 UTC — Canary halted; automated rollback failed to complete for subset of nodes due to partial manifest application
2024-11-07 10:48 UTC — Manual rollback triggered for affected hosts, traffic drained, fallback to previous model variant configured
2024-11-07 11:05 UTC — Traffic stabilized, decoding errors returned to baseline; incident declared mitigated
2024-11-07 11:40 UTC — Post-incident debug session: reproducer created using staged microbatch ordering and artificial prefetch delay
impact: Production impact was limited in absolute volume (~0.6% of traffic to /v1/generate across the two impacted regions during the window) but high-severity from a correctness perspective: corrupted outputs for end users and a small number of customer complaints. No data loss. Latency p95 increased by ~200ms for affected requests while the mismatch persisted.
root_cause: A timing/regression in the runtime prefetch logic allowed KV index updates (mapping token->KV offset) to be applied asynchronously and observed out-of-order by in-flight microbatches. During the regional weight merge, some nodes applied new weight shards while their KV index cache still referenced older shard offsets. The mismatch only manifests when microbatch ordering, prefetch, and partial shard apply interleave — a low-probability but real race condition introduced by a recent optimization to accelerate prefetch for long-context requests.
mitigation: Immediate: halted rollouts to remaining regions and enabled automatic fallback to previous model variant for client routes showing decoding failures
Immediate: drained and removed affected hosts from active pools, forced KV cache invalidation and rehydrate under strict ordering
Short-term: disabled the new prefetch ordering optimization under a feature flag until a deterministic update path is implemented
Short-term: added a guard in the weight-apply orchestration to block accepting traffic until KV index and weight shards are applied atomically
rollback_notes: Automated rollback timed out on ~4 hosts that had partially applied manifests; we performed targeted manual drain + reapply which successfully restored consistent state. Key step: forcing sequential KV index refresh immediately after weight swap before returning host to LB. Documented the manual sequence in the incident runbook for on-call.
lessons_learned: Async prefetch ordering introduces correctness risk in presence of non-atomic weight apply — performance optimizations must be validated against partial-apply scenarios
Canaries caught correctness issues but our automated rollback didn't handle partial manifest states robustly
Observability gap: we lacked a lightweight probe that checks KV index/weight shard affinity after a weight swap (added to follow-ups)
Runbooks should include explicit steps for forced KV cache invalidation and host rehydration
follow_up_actions: (P0) Implement atomic apply barrier: weight apply must include KV index update in same transaction or use a two-phase commit-style handshake
(P0) Expand Canary checks: add token-level decode sanity probe that runs immediately after weight apply and before traffic cutover
(P1) Rework prefetch opt to be idempotent and maintain versioned KV index pointers
(P1) Harden automated rollback to detect and recover partially applied manifests (add explicit recovery path rather than naive rollback)
(P2) Add telemetry: KV-index/version tags on spans and tokens for quick correlation in traces
(P2) Update deployment playbooks with explicit host drain, KV cache invalidate, and rehydrate steps
metrics: peak-error-rate: 7.2% for affected /v1/generate requests within 3-minute window on eu-west-1 hosts (local to canary group)
total-affected-traffic: ~0.6% of global /v1/generate requests during the incident window
p95-latency-increase: +200ms for impacted microbatches while mismatch persisted
MTTR: mitigated (traffic stable) in ~36 minutes from first alert
operational_playbook_changes: Add 'verify-kv-affinity' probe as a step in staged rollouts; fail fast if mismatch detected
When halting a rollout, immediately perform KV cache invalidation on nodes that may have partially applied manifests
Make partial-manifest recovery a documented, automated subroutine in the rollout controller
Add Slack alert channel routing for tokenization-corruption alerts to SRE and runtime teams
notes: Reproducer and unit tests added in runtime repo PR #4567. Coordinate with runtime/serving and release-engineering to schedule a safe rollout for the patched prefetch feature. Consider retro session with product teams owning customer impact communications. Customer Success notified of affected customers and remediation timeline.
